file_name: Lehmann et al. - 2022 - Designing AINA Intercultural Human Centered Design of an AI based Application for Supporting the Dia.txt

barriers.description: Socio-cultural differences and hierarchies prevented some user groups from expressing themselves honestly or at all during participatory design activities.
barriers.justification: This hindered the designers' ability to facilitate user involvement and manage user understanding, as they could not reliably gather authentic user input or feedback.
barriers.reference_excerpt: We ﬁrst had to learn, with the help of resident physicians, that certain interview settings did not produce the needed outcome because, due to socio-cultural differences, certain groups of people did not express themselves freely or at all in some settings, which is a major problem for participatory design methods.

barriers.description: The COVID-19 pandemic severely limited the availability and communication ability of relevant user groups, especially in Africa.
barriers.justification: This resource constraint directly impeded the designers' ability to facilitate user involvement and conduct interviews, thus limiting their capacity to understand the context of use and gather user requirements.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Another constraint is the currently active COVID-19 pandemic, which leads to severe limitations in the availability and communication ability of the relevant user groups, especially in Africa.

barriers.description: The inability to conduct on-site observations due to the COVID-19 pandemic prevented designers from studying user behavior in context.
barriers.justification: This hindered the operational workload of understanding the context of use and managing user understanding, as designers could not observe real-world practices and environments.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Since user behavior plays a crucial role in any technology, we wished to conduct additional on-site observations during the analysis and evaluation phases. Unfortunately, this was not possible due to the global COVID-19 pandemic.
